title: How Ann-Sophie Schälicke Redefines Inclusive Fashion With Clo
description:
Discover the story of Ann-Sophie Schälicke, a Germany-based designer redefining inclusive fashion with her brand A. Schaelicke. Through her participation in the Design Academy ADAPT program co-hosted by VORN – The Berlin Fashion Hub and Zalando, she discovered CLO, which enabled her to create adaptive designs for all body types. For Ann-Sophie, CLO isn’t just a tool; it’s the key to making her inclusive vision a reality.

Learn more about Design Academy ADAPT program: https://vorn-hub.com/design-academy-adapt-1
Learn more about A. Schaelicke: https://www.instagram.com/a.schaelicke/?hl=en
transcript: Hi, my name is Anne-Sophie Schellekern and I'm a German-based fashion designer dedicated to inclusive fashion. I saw the lack in the market, the accessibility, and the gaps not only in the products but also in the representation of the whole industry. And I wanted to close the gap and make shows with purpose so it's not just fabric, it's like an alley in your everyday life that supports and empowers you. My first step into adaptive fashion was my inclusive graduate collection in 2023. The name is Spotlight. I chose the name because I wanted to have the disabled community take center stage. I could stand in the spotlight. It stands out because of its innovative closures. I used magnets and bold font prints and futuristic silhouettes. The Design Academy is an educational program co-hosted by Vaughan, the Berlin Fashion Hub, and Zalando, the third edition, focused on creating innovation in adaptive fashion. The program gave me the opportunity to connect with like-minded designers and incredible industry experts and gave me the right tools for my work. And it's also where I discovered Claw. The most helpful tool of Claw for me is the virtual try-on with the avatar and the pose customization and the fabric simulation. So it allows me to adjust the body, types of my customers. So for example, seated position for wheelchair users. And the simulation allows me to adjust the fit for these specific needs. I use magnets and a special pattern cutting for the body position so that it looks flattering while standing and also while sitting. So for me, it shows more. And just the software, it's a tool that empowers me to design in a way that it aligns with my physical strengths. I don't need to use physical strength anymore and only focus on designing. Even in my most toughest moments when I was hospitalized, I could work on my adaptive pieces with Claw. So the tool gave me the freedom and the flexibility to do my work from anywhere. Claw has given me the tools to bring my vision to life with more precision and creativity. And I'm excited to see where it evolves in the future of adaptive fashion. I truly think I'm just at the beginning and I'm really excited to see where it takes me. To be continued We start at the end of the seminar. So we'll see you next time. And remember, the move is not the move. We are always moving forward. We will never stop. So stay positive and keep moving forward. We've been through hard times, and we have to keep moving forward. So stay когда we get through hard times. It's always a lot to do and a lot to do. We'll see you next time. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye. Bye.
markdown_content: ## Ann-Sophie Schälicke and Her Commitment to Inclusive Fashion This section introduces Ann-Sophie Schälicke, a German-based fashion designer focused on inclusive fashion, highlighting her motivation to address accessibility gaps in the fashion industry and her approach to creating purpose-driven designs that empower users. Ann-Sophie Schälicke identified significant gaps in the fashion market concerning accessibility and representation, motivating her to create inclusive fashion that goes beyond mere fabric to become an empowering aspect of everyday life. Her goal is to close these gaps by designing clothing that supports and uplifts its wearers, particularly those with disabilities. ## Spotlight: Ann-Sophie’s Inclusive Graduate Collection (2023) This section details Ann-Sophie's graduate collection "Spotlight," its focus on adaptive fashion, and its innovative design features, including closures, prints, and silhouettes. Ann-Sophie’s first major project in adaptive fashion was her 2023 graduate collection titled *Spotlight*. The name reflects her intention to bring the disabled community to center stage, symbolizing visibility and empowerment. The collection is distinguished by its use of innovative magnetic closures, bold font prints, and futuristic silhouettes. These elements combine to create garments that are not only functional but visually striking, challenging conventional fashion norms around disability. ## The Design Academy and Collaboration with Industry Experts This section explains the role of the Design Academy program in Ann-Sophie's development as a designer, highlighting its partnerships and focus on adaptive fashion innovation. The Design Academy is an educational initiative co-hosted by Vaughan, the Berlin Fashion Hub, and Zalando. Its third edition focused specifically on innovation in adaptive fashion, providing Ann-Sophie with access to a network of like-minded designers and industry experts. The program equipped her with advanced tools and knowledge essential for her work in inclusive design. It was through this program that she discovered the software tool Clo3D (referred to as "Claw" in the transcript). ## Clo3D as a Tool for Adaptive Fashion Design This section covers the technical features of Clo3D that support Ann-Sophie’s adaptive fashion work, including virtual try-on, avatar customization, fabric simulation, and how these features accommodate different body types and positions. Clo3D is a 3D garment visualization software that has proven instrumental for Ann-Sophie’s workflow. Key features she uses include: - **Virtual try-on with avatar and pose customization:** This allows her to simulate different body types, including seated positions for wheelchair users. - **Fabric simulation:** Enables precise adjustments to fabric fit and behavior, ensuring garments look flattering both when standing and sitting. - **Pattern cutting customization:** She uses magnetic closures combined with specialized pattern cutting to optimize garment fit and comfort for adaptive needs. These features empower her to design with precision and creativity while reducing the need for physical prototyping or strength, which is especially valuable during times when she is physically limited, such as hospital stays. ## Impact and Future Outlook in Adaptive Fashion This section reflects on the personal and professional impact of Clo3D on Ann-Sophie’s design process and her outlook on the future of adaptive fashion. Clo3D has granted Ann-Sophie significant freedom and flexibility, allowing her to work remotely and continue creating adaptive designs even during challenging personal circumstances. The software supports her vision with accuracy and creative freedom, enhancing her ability to meet the unique needs of her customers. She expresses excitement about the future evolution of adaptive fashion and views her current work as the beginning of a broader journey toward inclusivity and innovation in the industry.
